articles.excerpt: The Gradle team is excited to announce Gradle 9.9.3. Here are the highlights of this release: Performance improvements for Kotlin DSL compilation Test filtering for non-method JUnit Platform tests Wrapper settings preserved on upgrade Predefined groups in the Problems API Read the Release Notes We would like to thank the following community members for their contributions to this release of Gradle: Aurimas , devareddy05 , DragonFSKY , fru1tworld , Ivan Khanas , Jeremy Schoemaker , John Burns , Labh R Jethe , Marcin Mycek , monkey , Nelson Osacky , Roberto Perez Alcolea , Róbert Papp , SeungTaek Lim , Stefan Oehme , 万彬宇 , 한의준 . Upgrade instructions Switch your build to use Gradle 9.9.3 by updating your wrapper: ./gradlew :wrapper --gradle-version=9.9.3 && ./gradlew :wrapper See the Gradle 9.x upgrade guide to learn about deprecations, breaking changes and other considerations when upgrading. For Java, Groovy, Kotlin and Android compatibility, see the full compatibility notes . Reporting problems If you find a problem with this release, please file a bug on GitHub Issues adhering to our issue guidelines. If you're not sure you're encountering a bug, please use the forum . We hope you will build happiness with Gradle, and we look forward to your feedback via Twitter or on GitHub .
articles.summary: Gradle 9.9.3 améliore la compilation Kotlin DSL et ajoute des filtres de tests JUnit, avec des corrections mineures.

articles.title: Show HN: bouncemarket – a live prediction market game for a bouncing ball
articles.excerpt: a ball will fall. trade on where it lands. I made this game! Some technical details: The entire drop of the ball is simulated server-side, then streamed to each client as server-sent events with a small buffer. Every drop is deterministic from its starting position, so rounds can be replayed exactly for later analysis, but tiny variations in starting position can change the ultimate outcome. There's some AI traders to keep the market moving, but they drop out in any round that has more than five people. They operate using a naive set of rules that I wrote for them, so they're not too hard to beat -- it's when the market is full of real people that it gets tricky. Curious to get feedback on anything you would change, and especially whether the mechanics were clear right away or not.
articles.summary: Un jeu de marché prédictif en direct simule une balle rebondissante côté serveur et diffuse ses mouvements aux joueurs pour parier sur son atterrissage.

articles.title: Show HN: I restored Palm's last device, and brought its OS to other platforms
articles.excerpt: webOS Community Edition 3.2.0 is the first OTA Update for Palm/HP's TouchPad, modernizing a 15-year old device. Lunacy is its sibling: the webOS experience, and apps, on Android. Luna DE is a developer tool that brings the webOS app contract to Mac, Windows and Linux as a SDK-compatible Electron app.
